title: Fix : Make Volume Units persistent to prevent container crashes
body:
Fixes: #27331

Behaviour : When a multiple containers are managed by systemd in `separate cgroup buckets`, which uses the same volume created by image-drive crashes when the first container got killed, it breaks the volumes for all the other containers, the remaining containers lose access to all the shared files and throw a `Socket not connected` error

Root Cause : Quadlet generate `.Volume` units as scripts that exit without mounting. The first container to start is forced to spawn the `fuse-overlayfs` mount process inside its own `systemd cgroup`, which systemd destroys when that specific container stops.

Solution : Updated Quadlet to generate `.volume` units as persistent services (`RemainAfterExit=yes`) that explicitly execute podman volume mount and unmount. This safely isolates the `FUSE mount process` within the volume's dedicated cgroup, completely decoupling its lifecycle from individual containers.

Also since it isolates the process of  `fuse-overlays` by making the `.volume` alive the similar approah is followed for `.network` and `.image` and update the tests accordingly

comments.body: I thought about moving fuse-overlayfs to a separate cgroup but it doesn't make much sense as conmon and pasta because it is owned by a layer, not a container.  Multiple containers can reuse the same fuse-overlayfs mount.

> I thought about moving fuse-overlayfs to a separate cgroup but it doesn't make much sense as conmon and pasta because it is owned by a layer, not a container. Multiple containers can reuse the same fuse-overlayfs mount.

Well that is my point, the fuse-overlay process must be moved outside the systemd unit cgroup so it does not get killed when the service which start it is not stopped. Like the pause process, or the rootless netns pasta process it must be moved to its own scope under the user slice I believe.

> Well that is my point, the fuse-overlay process must be moved outside the systemd unit cgroup so it does not get killed when the service which start it is not stopped. Like the pause process, or the rootless netns pasta process it must be moved to its own scope under the user slice I believe.

we could perhaps reuse the same cgroup as the pause process, as anyway we lose the userns+mountns reference once pause exits

> 
> we could perhaps reuse the same cgroup as the pause process, as anyway we lose the userns+mountns reference once pause exits

doesn't relying on the pause process cgroup might contradict the upcoming `PODMAN_NO_PAUSE_PROCESS=1` architecture?

Moving the `fuse-overlayfs` process into its own separate, independent scope under user.slice is what seems correct. I need to rework the whole PR, if the suggested bottom approach sounds correct I can start working on this ??
 
However, to implement this cleanly, we will need an upstream PR. Currently, libpod doesn't know the `FUSE daemon's PID` because `containers/storage` handles the execution and only returns the mount path.

Here is the implementation path I propose:

1. Upstream PR (containers/storage): Modify the storage layer so it captures and returns the PID of the FUSE daemon alongside the mount path.
2. Podman Core (libpod / common): Once we have the PID natively, we duplicate the existing pause/pasta logic and make a native `DBus` call to assign that PID to a new, dedicated `podman-storage.scope`
